Earlier this year, rumors surfaced that the redesigned Health app would debut in iOS 26.4. That plan was subsequently pushed back, and even some time after iOS 27's release, the rewritten Health app has still not materialized.

With the next-generation Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 expected to launch next month, it's worth exploring whether the related new features might be announced at the same event.

Precedent

First, it's necessary to look back at why these features are very likely to be announced in September. You might think: "Shouldn't all software be released in June?" — but in fact, there is indeed precedent in this regard.

Features like watchOS 9's Low Power Mode, watchOS 11's sleep apnea detection, and watchOS 26's hypertension notifications did not require the latest hardware to work, but all were only officially announced in September.

Therefore, based on the above reasons, Apple is very likely to wait until September to announce the latest Health app upgrade, even though these features may not necessarily require a brand-new Apple Watch to function.

Still Time

Before WWDC27, Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman warned that the Health app upgrade, codenamed "Project Mulberry," might not appear at the WWDC keynote. He turned out to be right:

Does this mean Project Mulberry will definitely appear at the September event? Not necessarily. However, given that there is precedent for announcing features in September, and we already know this project's launch may come later than WWDC, the chances of a September debut look quite high — though in the end it may have to wait until October, arriving alongside iOS 27.1.

Feature Recap

With so many factors involved, rumors are flying thick and fast. You may have heard about a standalone Health+ service, featuring videos personally filmed by doctors. However, according to reports, those plans have been scaled back, and the features will be integrated into the existing Health app experience.

That said, two things are already fairly clear: first, an AI health coach will be introduced, offering health advice based on your Health app data; second, real-time exercise and other health-related task guidance will be provided through the camera. Another key aspect of this upgrade is that the Health app will adopt a brand-new design, making it easier for users to understand their data.

Beyond that, we'll have to wait and see. Personally, I'm really looking forward to better ways to organize and understand my Apple Health data.
